key_insight: An efficient distillation + parameter-transfer recipe makes it practical to convert pretrained softmax‑attention transformers into hybrid linear‑attention/RNN architectures, preserving accuracy while enabling extremely long contexts with much lower compute and memory.
problem_solved: Pretraining hybrid Transformer/RNN models from scratch for long‑context tasks is prohibitively expensive; existing conversion methods are inefficient or degrade performance, limiting adoption for very long sequences.
method: Design a compact distillation protocol that transfers knowledge from pretrained softmax‑attention blocks into linear/RNN blocks with targeted losses and parameter mappings.
Propose hybrid architecture choices and conversion rules (which layers to convert, gating/skip connections) that retain modeling capacity while enabling O(n) memory/compute.
Empirically validate across very long context benchmarks, showing large throughput/memory gains with minimal performance drop.
impact: Enables practitioners to reuse large pretrained models rather than retrain hybrids from scratch, drastically reducing compute and memory for long‑context applications (document search, code, multi‑hour audio, agents). This makes deployment of extremely long‑context models practical and cost‑effective.

paper_title: Hybrid Linear Attention Done Right: Efficient Distillation and Effective Architectures for Extremely Long Contexts
paper_authors: Yingfa Chen, Zhen Leng Thai, Zihan Zhou, Zhu Zhang, Xingyu Shen
